summary: VPCE secondary DNS failover stalls control-plane heartbeats and triggers serving-node evictions for FinSure private deploy
description: Customers reported intermittent serving-node disconnects and model failures for FinSure's private VPC endpoint. Nodes lost control-plane heartbeats for ~20-40s, causing the autoscaler to mark them unhealthy and trigger temporary evictions. This appears correlated with DNS failover events on the customer's VPCE resolver path when the secondary (on-prem forwarding) takes precedence.
impact: Ongoing request errors and transient 5xxs for FinSure production traffic in us-east-1. Multiple serving nodes evicted and restarted, increased tail latency for short windows. Revenue-impacting for critical payment flows; P1 severity.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer uses VPCE DNS with primary=AWS-resolver and secondary=on-prem DNS forwarder (over a private link).
2) Simulate secondary DNS becoming responsive first by introducing higher TCP latency to primary or blocking UDP53 to primary resolver from subnet (customer side).
3) Observe control-plane gRPC keepalive failures from serving nodes to control-plane at approximately keepalive interval + retransmit window (~20-40s).
4) Check autoscaler logs for health check TTL expiry and node eviction entries.

comments: 2026-03-12T21:05Z - Maya Chen: Customer reported spikes in 5xxs and confirms topology: VPCE -> VPC route -> Transit -> on-prem DNS forwarder. Primary AWS resolver responds intermittently under their egress policy.

2026-03-12T21:20Z - Rafael Ortega (SRE): Initial hypothesis: DNS resolution ordering flips to secondary (over TCP) which returns stale CNAME records with longer TTL; gRPC connections attempt name resolution and experience TCP handshake delay leading to keepalive misses.

2026-03-13T02:14Z - FinSure NetOps (customer): We deployed a temporary ACL to prefer AWS resolver for control-plane FQDNs; observed immediate reduction in edge evictions. Will keep ACL for 24h while Redwood tests patch.

2026-03-13T22:50Z - Rafael Ortega: Deployed control-plane DNS failover tolerance patch (v1.2.3) to staging; patch implements aggressive resolver prioritization, faster fallback and keepalive jitter. Scheduling prod deploy tonight.
2026-03-14T00:10Z - Customer (FinSure): Observed one last transient eviction at 23:57, no further sustained incidents. Monitoring continues.
investigation_notes: Packet captures from customer show UDP53 to primary resolver dropped intermittently (egress ACL), client retried via TCP to secondary causing ~150-300ms extra latency.

Control-plane uses hostname-based TLS pinning; when resolution returns via secondary, CNAME ordering returned non-canonical name triggering extra SRV lookups and a slow path in our client resolver library.

Our gRPC keepalive config tolerates short packet loss but not the combined effect of TCP fallback + SRV chase; observed keepalive retransmits reach 12s before grpc library marks as missed and then 30s total to eviction window.
Related past ticket SUP-93188 described an intermittent VPCE DNS cache staleness — different root cause but similar customer-visible symptom.
resolution: Applied a two-pronged remediation: 1) Customer applied an egress ACL to prefer AWS resolver for control-plane hostnames (immediate mitigation). 2) Redwood rolled out control-plane client patch (v1.2.3) that short-circuits SRV/CNAME chase during resolver fallback, adds resolver-priority hints for VPCE paths, and increases keepalive jitter. Prod rollout completed 2026-03-13 22:50 UTC. Post-deploy monitoring shows no further sustained evictions.
resolution_deploys: customer ACL change: FinSure NetOps prefer-aws-resolver rule (2026-03-12T21:30:00Z)
follow_up_tasks: 1) Engineering: Add telemetry to trace resolver path and indicate TCP fallback events (owner: Rafael, due: 2026-03-20).
2) DX/Docs: Update private-deploy runbook to recommend VPCE egress rules for control-plane fqdn (owner: Ana Lopez, due: 2026-03-18).
3) Product: Consider making resolver-priority configurable for private deployments (product ticket creation pending).
4) Support: Reach out to other private-tier customers who use VPCE with on-prem forwarders and offer the patch/mitigation (owner: CS team).
notes: Root cause: interplay of VPCE resolver ordering, customer egress policy causing UDP loss to primary, and our client resolver SRV/CNAME chase that amplifies TCP fallback latency leading to gRPC keepalive misses. Fix combined customer ACL and server-side client tolerance improvements.
public_update_template: We identified intermittent control-plane heartbeat failures caused by DNS failover behaviour in a private VPCE topology. A patch has been deployed and the customer applied a mitigative egress rule. If you are on a private deployment and use on-prem DNS forwarding, please contact support to verify resolver order or to obtain the client-side patch.
